catalog_citation: Donohue, Mark. 1997. Tone systems in New Guinea. Linguistic Typology 1(3): 347-386.

catalog_quote: 5.4. Languages reported to be or likely to be tonal languages. Many languages are either reported to display tonal behaviour, or [...] from available wordlists to be likely to either use some sort of sup[ra]segmental factors in differentiating words, or to have an unaccountabl[y] large number of homonyms amongst their basic vocabulary. Due [to] lack of data, however, the nature of the tonal system present i[n the] languages concerned cannot be given in detail. [...] For details of the evidence or reports supporting the claim [that] they might be tonal, see Donohue (1993). The languages thought [to be] tonal include the following: Karon Dori (West Papua family), Tarungga[re] (East Geelvink Bay), Wodani, Moni, Uhunduni (Wissel Lakes) Ketengban, Naltya (Mek family), Foau, Dabra (East Lake Plains), Rawo (Sko phylum), Yaqay (Marind family) [...]

It is a typological journal article on tone (Linguistic Typology 1), not a comparative-historical work; 'phonology-article' is the closer class. the Internet Archive URL not re-downloaded (file already on. | scanned p. 374 sec. 5.4 reads '..The languages thought to[be] tonal include the following: Karon Dori (West Papua family), Tarunggar[e] (East Geelvink Bay), Wodani, Moni, Uhunduni (Wissel Lakes) Ketengban, Naltya (Mek family), Foau, Dabra (East Lake Plains), Rawo (Sko phylum), Yaqay (Marind family)..'; the searcher's bracketed restoratio…
new_statements.relation_note: Lists 'Foau, Dabra (East Lake Plains)' among languages 'reported to be or likely to be tonal'; no tone inventory, nothing on stress; evidence referred to Donohue 1993 (unpublished).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Dabra (Taworta/Diebroud area lect) is reported or inferred from wordlists to be tonal; nature of the system unknown.
new_statements.exceptions: author states the nature of the tonal system 'cannot be given in detail' for all languages in this list
new_statements.identity_note: 'Dabra' is the East Lakes Plain lect recorded at Magambilis that Voorhoeve 1975 (PL C-38: 412) calls 'very closely related [to Taworta-Aero], and perhaps dialects of one language'; Clouse 1997 lists Dabra (100 speakers) beside Taworta in the East Lakes Plain family; Glottolog 5.3 files the name Dabra under tawo1244 (name search 'Dabra' returns only tawo1244/lake1255); Yoder 2020: 10 cautions that Taburta [tbp] and Waritai are both spoken at Dabra village. Not ISO dba (= Bangime). [name in source: Dabra (East Lake Plains); pages 374 (sec. 5.4)]

new_statements.quote: Bromley notes that Dabra seems to be tonal; it further appears that all the Lake Plain languages except Dabra and Baburiwa have implosive stops. Baburiwa has nasal vowels. All the word lists contains only three personal pronouns: I, we, and you (sing.).

new_statements.locator: p. 412 (p. 68 of the copy consulted), sec. 2.6.2.2.11.1.4 'Notes on the East Lake Plain and Central Lake Plain Families', first sentence; lines 3339-3341 (extracted text output is letter-spaced, e.g. 'Broml ey not e s t hat Dabra s eems to be t onal'; quote given with the spacing normalised, wording unchanged)
new_statements.relation_note: Tone: 'Dabra seems to be tonal' (Bromley's observation). Stress: nothing. The preceding sec. 2.6.2.2.11.1.3 (p. 412) lists the four East Lake Plain wordlists (Taworta-Aero, Dabra, Foau) and repeats that Taworta-Aero and Dabra are 'perhaps dialects of one language'.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand impressionistic report (Bromley, via Voorhoeve) that Dabra, the Taworta-area East Lakes Plain variety, 'seems to be tonal'; no tone inventory, no minimal pairs, nothing on stress or accent placement.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the accompanying segmental note is that Dabra (with Baburiwa) lacks the implosive stops found in the other Lake Plain lists
new_statements.identity_note: PASS-1 WORK, added: a tone remark pass 1 missed (pass-1 work 1001 was recorded as 'nothing; p. 411..'). The remark is about 'Dabra' = Voorhoeve's no. 88 (village Magambilis), which the same page calls 'very closely related' to Taworta-Aero, 'perhaps dialects of one language'; Ethnologue/Glottolog/TransNewGuinea/ASJP all file Dabra under Diebroud [tbp] = tawo1244 (no separate glottocode), Clouse 1997 keeps it as a third East Lakes Plain lect, Yoder 2020 says Taburta (and Waritai) are what is spoken at Dabra. Data basis: M. Bromley's missionary survey wordlists (p. 353 'Bromley's lists'; p. 411 'lists in the Lake Plain languages made available to him by M. Bromley'). This is almost certainly the print origin of Ethnologue's unsourced 'tonal' and of Donohue 1993/1997's 'Dabra (East Lake Plains).. likely to be tonal'.

sources.citation: Clouse, Duane A. 1997. Towards a reconstruction and reclassification of the Lakes Plain languages of Irian Jaya. In Karl Franklin (ed.), Papers in Papuan linguistics No. 2 (Pacific Linguistics A-85), 133-236. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Taworta is explicitly excluded from the study (p.134: 'The languages in the Lakes Plain not included in the study were Kwerisa and Papasena.. and Taworta, Dabra and Foau in the East Lakes Plain Family.. The data available for these languages was considered insufficient'); no Taworta word list in Appendix 3; Taworta appears only in the reclassification tree (p.155). Family-level remarks only: p.152 'Tone is a prominent feature of all Lakes Plain languages'; p.160 stress 'has not been found to be contrastive in any of the Lakes Plain languages to date' -- neither rests on Taworta data.
